title: Ruth
author: The author is not named; Jewish tradition has often associated the book with Samuel.
date: Set in the time of the judges; written later to show God's providential work in David's family line.
audience: Israel, showing God's covenant kindness through ordinary faithfulness and His providence in the line of David.
historicalSetting: Ruth takes place during the dark period of the judges and follows Naomi, Ruth, and Boaz as God works through loss, loyalty, redemption, and covenant kindness.
keyVerse: Ruth 4:14 — "Blessed be Yahweh, who has not left you today without a near kinsman."
christFocus: Boaz as kinsman-redeemer points toward Christ, who redeems His people. Ruth also stands in the line leading to David and ultimately to Jesus Christ.
outline: Naomi and Ruth's loss and loyalty — Ruth 1
The genealogy leading to David — Ruth 4
